subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Nova Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <ajordan@novapay.com>, Priya Shah <priya@novapay.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Nova Payments

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points you confirmed
- Production latency variability during peak settlement windows (95th pct spikes to ~700ms, target <200ms)
- Sensitive customer data requires strict isolation and auditability for payment flows
- Current infra (self-hosted on GCP single project) struggles to scale predictably for daily batch loads and peak TPS bursts

Current stack and constraints - Frontend: Node.js + Next.js; Backend: Java + Spring; Model inference currently in a hybrid setup (on-prem for some regulated models, cloud for others)
- ML workloads today: routing / fraud scoring and contextual NLU for dispute resolution; average concurrent inference sessions ~120 across two regions, expected to grow to ~600 in 12 months
- Compliance: SOC 2 in review; PCI scope applies to primary payment flows; require customer-managed KMS for encryption of any persisted model state or logs

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit - Predictable throughput: sustain 500 TPS steady with 1–2x burst for peak windows
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pools per environment (prod/stage) and no co-mingling with other tenants
- Autoscaling & burst: ability to configure scheduled scale-up for known batch windows and on-demand burst capacity for unexpected spikes
- Observability & audit: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and audit logs retention for 12 months

Recommendations and next steps
1) Pricing & sizing: attached is a preliminary sizing and pricing deck (rio-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf) and a small MAU estimate sheet (mau-estimates.xlsx). Rafael will review further sizing details.
2) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60-minute Dedicated tech session to validate networking/KMS requirements and quantify steady-state/peak GPU needs (proposed: Thu 3/4 or Fri 3/5). Please share any blackout windows.
3) Compliance checklist: we’ll collect Nova Payments’ SOC/PCI contacts to run the security questionnaire and scope the Private controls needed.
4) Mutual action plan: if we align on fit after the tech deep-dive, we can deliver a pilot Dedicated cluster for a 30-day validation with SLA targets and rollback policies.

Please reply with any corrections to the above and confirm availability for the tech session. Happy to make adjustments to the MAU assumptions if you have more detailed usage slices.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rio-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf (PDF, 212 KB)
Attachment: mau-estimates.xlsx (XLSX, 28 KB)

From: Alex Jordan <ajordan@novapay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@novapay.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Nova Payments

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

- The 500 TPS steady target is accurate as our planning baseline; during monthly settlement windows we can see sustained bursts closer to 1,000 TPS for ~30–45 minutes. Can Redwood support 2x burst over steady for short windows?
- For isolation: we need dedicated pools per product line (payments, disputes, analytics) — not just per environment. Is that doable within a single Dedicated contract?
- On KMS: yes, customer-managed KMS is mandatory for production. We also need HSM-backed key options for specific flows.

We’re available 3/4 after 10am PT for the technical deep-dive. Rafael — looping you in for sizing follow-up (I believe Rafael did a sizing for a similar finance customer recently).

On the attachments: saw the pricing PDF; will take a pass and send back redlines by EOD Wednesday.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Nova Payments

Alex — great questions, thanks. Short answers here and actions below.

- Burst capacity: yes — Redwood Dedicated supports configurable burst policies up to 3x steady-state for short windows via reserved burst pools and on-demand burst allocation. We’ll confirm exact sizing options in the tech deep-dive.
- Dedicated pools per product line: doable. We can map GPU pools to product lines under a single Dedicated contract; each pool can have isolation controls and separate autoscaling policies.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS integrations (GCP/AWS/Azure) and can integrate with HSM-backed stores for key wrapping on a per-flow basis.

Action items
- Rafael: can you validate the attached MAU estimates against a 3x burst scenario and add recommended GPU VM families + node counts by Thu 3/4 EOD? (cc’d)
- Alex / Priya: please confirm if Thu 3/4 10:30–11:30 PT works for the tech deep-dive or propose an alternate.
- Marissa: I’ll prepare a short pilot proposal and run the internal SLA exceptions checklist to confirm achievable latency SLOs for the pilot.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
